speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to begin my assessment, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they worsened suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest, especially with diplopia upon looking up or down, strongly suggests a neuromuscular junction disorder. Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty swallowing or speaking?

REQUEST TEST: Repeat_Nerve_Conduction_Study
REQUEST TEST: Single_Fiber_Electromyography

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.

The normal results from the nerve conduction studies and single-fiber EMG effectively rule out primary neuromuscular junction disorders like Lambert-Eaton or myasthenia gravis, as these tests would typically show abnormalities in those conditions. Given the specific symptoms of diplopia on gaze and activity-induced weakness, please describe your medical history regarding thyroid issues or autoimmune conditions, and tell me if you have ever experienced any respiratory difficulties or chest pain.
